book.spell_guidebook.buildaspell.advance:
The first five slots can also be cast directly with their own keybinds (Cast Spell 1 through Cast Spell 5), bypassing the ring entirely for faster access.\
\
The remaining slots are reached through the ring itself.\
\
Configure these keybinds in the Controls menu under the 'Build a Spell' category.

The Ability Ring is a radial menu for quick spell selection.\
\
Press V to open it and hover over a slot to select that spell.\
\
The ring supports 10 spell slots, each holding one Spell Rune.\
\
Release V to select the highlighted spell for casting.

The server config lives in a 'buildaspell' folder, split across general.toml, deliveries.toml, effects.toml, modifiers.toml, and wands.toml.\
\
Between them they control global settings: the mana cost multiplier, default spell power, per-delivery/effect/modifier toggles and cost multipliers, damage multipliers for offensive effects, the maximum number of portals per player, and the list of blocks allowed for Conjure.\
\
These server values sync to clients automatically on login.

Server operators manage player mana with /buildaspell mana (alias /cbas mana): mana set <amount> [target] sets mana to a value, mana add <amount> [target] adds mana, mana get [target] shows current mana, and mana stats [target] shows max mana, regen, and spell power.\
\
The target is optional and defaults to you.\
\
These require operator permissions.

The /buildaspell spell suite (alias /cbas spell) manages spells: spell export <slot> prints the spell in a slot as a shareable code, spell copy <slot> copies that code to your clipboard, and spell import <slot> <code> loads a code into a slot.\
\
spell list [target] shows a player's unlocked components, and spell combo <id> <slot> builds a known combo into a slot.\
\
These require operator permissions.

Use /buildaspell spell export <slot> (alias /cbas spell export <slot>) to print the spell in that slot as a Base64-encoded string.\
\
This string can be shared with other players, posted online, or saved as a backup.\
\
The export captures the complete spell configuration including all components and their order.

Press I to open the Import Spell screen.\
\
Paste a Base64 spell string into the text field and confirm to load it onto a Blank Rune in your inventory.\
\
This allows you to use spells created by other players or restore backed-up configurations.

Void Rifts are opened by the Void Rift combo: a teleportation working given persistence and breadth.\
\
The exact recipe is yours to discover in the Spell Builder.\
\
Each portal must be named and can be linked to any other named portal you have created.

Portals are linked by name: dial a destination portal's name to connect them.\
\
Connected portals work bidirectionally.\
\
Void Rifts work across dimensions, letting you create instant travel networks between the Overworld, Nether, and End.\
\
The server config can limit the maximum portals per player.

Void Rifts are stable portals created by the Void Rift combo spell.\
\
Each rift is a swirling gateway: step into one and it carries you to the destination you have dialed, even across dimensions.

Every spell starts with a Delivery Method: this determines how the spell reaches its target.\
\
Then add Effects to define what the spell does (damage, heal, teleport, etc.), and Modifiers to customize behavior (increase power, add pierce, etc.).\
\
Components are ordered left to right.

The Spell Builder shows the total mana cost of your current spell configuration in real time.\
\
As you add or remove components, the cost updates automatically.\
\
The cost accounts for all base costs, modifiers, and any server-configured cost multipliers.\
\
Spells can have up to 30 components.

The Spell Builder is the core interface for creating spells.\
\
Press G to open it while holding a Blank Rune.\
\
The interface presents a drag-and-drop workspace where you assemble your spell from a delivery method, effects, and modifiers.
Certain spell configurations resonate into something far greater than their parts.\
\
Hidden combinations wait in these pages, and rumor hints at what each one becomes.\
\
The Summoning arts are said to call iron guardians, swarming vexes, skeleton archers, and ranks of armored vindicators.\
\
Movement and Force can tear open a black hole, raise a roaring tornado, grant lasting flight, or snap you free in a desperate escape.\
\
World Manipulation can drown the land beneath water or lava, while Teleportation can split open a void rift or conjure an instant fortress.\
\
The exact recipe for each stays sealed until you study the spell effect it draws upon.\
\
Read an effect's chapter in full, and the combinations built on it reveal themselves here on their own.

Flame and blast, spread wide rather than piled high, settle over the land as a burning rain.\
\
A rain of small fireballs falls across the area, leaving lingering flames burning on the ground where they land.\
\
Lighter and wider than a Meteor Strike, it blankets a broad zone in fire.\
\
Increased Area widens the storm.

Hurl fire and ruin at the heavens with enough raw power behind it, and the heavens hurl it back.\
\
A volley of huge fireballs rains from the sky onto the target area, each detonating in an explosion and setting the ground ablaze.\
\
Increased Area widens the bombardment and adds more meteors; Increased Power makes each blast bigger, capping at two stacks.

A caster who weaves together every way a body can rise and fall gently may, for a time, forget the ground entirely.\
\
This combo grants the caster the ability to fly freely for its duration.\
\
Best used with Self delivery; Prolonged and Increased Power extend the flight time.

Stack every art of vanishing you know into one desperate working and the spell will choose your exit for you.\
\
When cast, this combo whisks you to a random safe spot far from danger: potentially hundreds of blocks away.\
\
Not even the caster knows where they will land, which makes it impossible to follow or counter.

A single spring, given room to spread and taught to leap from pool to pool, becomes a deluge.\
\
Water source blocks are placed rapidly across a wide area, filling in terrain and creating a massive body of water.\
\
Use with caution: this can dramatically reshape the landscape.

Set the deluge itself alight, a grander and costlier working than the flood, and molten rock pours out in water's place.\
\
This is the most demanding combo in the game, and the resulting lava flow is devastating to both entities and terrain.

Where conjured water meets an upward shove across a broad footing, the ground erupts.\
\
A column of water blasts upward from the target, hurling every entity caught above it high into the air.\
\
The jet is purely visual and leaves no water behind, making it a handy mobility tool or a brutal fall-trap.\
\
Increased Area widens the eruption.

Somewhere in the meeting of inward force and folded space, a gravitational singularity waits to be found.\
\
Widen the working generously: a narrow spell cannot hold it.\
\
The Black Hole pulls all nearby entities toward a single point with immense force.\
\
One of the most powerful area control combos.

Bitter cold, a hungry wind, room to rage, and time to linger: give a storm all four and it will answer.\
\
A freezing storm settles over the area, chilling every creature caught inside while the wind drags them toward its heart.\
\
Increased Area widens the storm and Duration prolongs the freeze.

Draw your foes in and hurl them at the sky in the same breath, over a wide enough stretch of ground, and the wind itself takes over.\
\
Entities caught in the area are pulled inward and launched skyward repeatedly, creating a deadly vortex of wind and force.

Conjuring that is asked to cover ground and to endure will raise walls instead of blocks.\
\
The fortress is a hollow dome of impenetrable magical barrier raised around the caster; it fades away on its own, lasting longer with each Duration stack.\
\
Excellent for creating instant shelter in emergencies.

A translocation held open long enough, and stretched wide enough, stops being a journey and becomes a door.\
\
Void Rift portals allow instant travel between any two linked locations, even across dimensions.\
\
See the Portal System entry in Advanced Systems for full details.

Mending magic, poured out over ground instead of a body and left to keep working, consecrates the earth itself.\
\
The ground is hallowed, wrapping every player who stands within it (yourself included) in a protective ward of regeneration, resistance, and absorption.\
\
Hostile mobs are never sheltered.\
\
Increased Power strengthens the ward and Duration makes it last longer.

Summoning is a school of pairings: what you weave alongside the calling decides what answers.\
\
Bolster the calling with restorative magic and a friendly Iron Golem answers.\
\
Lace it instead with violence and spatial trickery, and a swarm of allied Vexes flickers into being to harry nearby enemies.

Call with the storm's own fury and a squad of Skeleton archers rises to your banner.\
\
Pour raw, widened power into a violent calling and ranks of allied Vindicators march out instead.\
\
Both armies fight for you, and both take real strength to raise: weak workings summon nothing.

Drive a blast downward into the earth across a wide enough span and the ground itself convulses.\
\
A shockwave tears across the ground, damaging and heaving entities skyward while rupturing the terrain itself.\
\
Increased Area widens the quake's reach.

A bolt is an instant; a storm is a bolt given breadth and time.\
\
Drifting storm clouds gather over the area and rain down real lightning over time.\
\
Increased Area calls more clouds across a wider front, while Duration keeps the storm raging longer.
book.spell_guidebook.buildaspell.deliver: Cast projectiles can be enhanced with several modifiers: Accelerate increases travel speed, Pierce allows the projectile to pass through entities and hit multiple targets, Bounce makes it ricochet off surfaces, and Split divides it into multiple projectiles.

The Cast delivery method fires a magical projectile in the direction the caster is looking.\
\
At 25 base mana, it offers a good balance between cost and versatility.\
\
The projectile travels in a straight line and triggers on the first entity or block it hits.
Place spell runes on the ground

The Rune delivery method inscribes a glowing spell rune on the ground at your feet.\
\
The rune charges for about a second, then releases its spell effects on its own.\
\
Each Duration modifier extends the charge time, letting you tune when it goes off.

Runes are timed charges: drop one and move, and it detonates where you stood.\
\
Use damage or status runes to cover a retreat, or healing runes to bless ground you are about to fight on.\
\
For a rune that waits for an enemy instead of a timer, see the Trap delivery.

The Self delivery method targets the caster directly.\
\
It is the cheapest delivery method at 5 base mana cost, making it ideal for buff spells like Shield, Speed, Heal, and Invisibility.\
\
The spell takes effect instantly on the caster with no projectile or targeting required.
Target what you are looking at

The Sight delivery method performs a raycast from the caster's eyes to the block or entity under the crosshair, up to 20 blocks away.\
\
It costs 15 base mana and is perfect for precise, targeted spells.\
\
If nothing solid is under the crosshair, the spell lands at the far end of the ray instead.
The next hit applies the spell

Touch holds the spell ready in your hand instead of casting it right away.\
\
The spell is released the next time you strike an entity in melee or right-click an entity or block.\
\
If you do not use the charge in time, it fades away.

Touch is the cheapest way to land a spell exactly on a target, with no projectile to dodge.\
\
It pairs naturally with damage and status effects: charge the spell, then deliver it with a sword swing.\
\
Only one charge is held at a time, so casting Touch again replaces the previous one.

The Tracking delivery method fires a homing projectile that seeks out the nearest valid target.\
\
At 35 base mana it is the most expensive delivery method, but its ability to lock onto and follow targets makes it devastating in combat.\
\
The projectile adjusts its trajectory mid-flight to home in on its target.
An armed rune that triggers on approach

Trap places an armed rune on the surface you are looking at.\
\
After a short arming delay, it waits and then triggers the moment any living creature other than you steps within range.\
\
When sprung, it casts the spell at the rune and vanishes.

Unlike a Rune, which fires on its own after charging, a Trap waits for a victim and persists until something approaches or its lifetime runs out.\
\
Use it to guard doorways and chokepoints, or to set ambushes with offensive effects.\
\
The trigger radius and lifetime are configurable.
book.spell_guidebook.buildaspell.getting:
The three enchantments available at the Arcane Altar are Mana Pool (increases maximum mana), Mana Regeneration (speeds mana recovery), and Spell Power (amplifies spell effects).\
\
Each enchantment can be applied multiple times with increasing cost per tier.

The Arcane Altar is the enchanting station for Build-A-Spell.\
\
Unlike the vanilla Enchanting Table, the Arcane Altar supports three unique enchantments with no level cap by default: server owners can set a cap for each enchantment in the config.

A Blank Rune fills with essence from two sources.\
\
The first is defeating enemies, where bosses such as the Ender Dragon and Wither grant far more than common mobs.\
\
The second is casting spells, where costlier spells yield more essence.\
\
Once it holds enough, the rune automatically transforms into a Spell Rune in your inventory.

The Blank Rune is the foundation of all spell creation.\
\
It gathers magical essence as you practice magic: every hostile mob you slay and every spell you cast feeds power into the rune.

A Blank Rune needs 200 essence to become a Spell Rune.\
\
Each hostile mob you slay grants 1 essence, while bosses such as the Ender Dragon and Wither grant 50.\
\
Casting grants essence equal to a quarter of the mana spent: 0.25 per point.\
\
A server admin can retune every one of these values, or switch off cast progression entirely.
A rune inscribed with a spell

A Spell Rune is a Blank Rune that has been inscribed with a spell using the Spell Builder.\
\
Each Spell Rune holds a single spell configuration and can be assigned to one of 10 slots in the Ability Ring for quick casting.

Open the Spell Builder (G key) to design your spell on a Blank Rune.\
\
Once saved, the Blank Rune transforms into a Spell Rune.\
\
Assign it to your Ability Ring (V key) and use the Cast Spell key or direct slot keybinds to cast.

Worn Wand: a stick at the bottom, a redstone dust in the center, a gold ingot on top, with a purple dye and a cyan dye on either side of the center.\
\
Carved Wand: combine a Worn Wand with a Spell Rune.\
\
Runic Wand: surround a Carved Wand with a Nether Star, a Dragon Head, and Spell Runes filling the remaining slots.
Hand-held casting foci that discount mana and cast on right-click

A wand is a focus you keep in hand while you cast.\
\
Hold any wand and it discounts the mana cost of every spell you cast; right-click and it casts the spell currently selected in your Ability Ring, with no keybind needed.\
\
There are three tiers, each stronger than the last.\
\
Holding two wands never stacks: only the strongest tier applies.

The Worn Wand is the cheap starter: a modest mana discount and a small boost to Spell Power.\
\
The Carved Wand deepens both the discount and the Spell Power bonus, amplifying your effects further.\
\
The Runic Wand is the endgame focus, with the steepest discount and the greatest Spell Power.\
\
Every one of these values is set by the server config, so an admin can tune the numbers to taste.
An introduction to the Arcane Codex

The Arcane Codex is your guide to mastering the art of spell creation.\
\
Within these pages you will find everything you need to craft powerful spells, from basic rune creation to advanced combo techniques.

Navigate the node graph by clicking on category icons at the top.\
\
Each node represents a topic: click it to read its pages.\
\
Some entries are hidden until you have read their prerequisites.\
\
Explore freely and discover the secrets of magic.
book.spell_guidebook.buildaspell.mana_sy:
Mana Pool determines your maximum mana capacity (default: 100).\
\
Mana Regen controls how quickly mana restores (default: 5/sec).\
\
Both can be increased through enchantments at the Arcane Altar and are exposed as entity attributes for cross-mod compatibility.

Spell Power scales the magnitude of your spell effects: more Power means more damage, healing, and force (default: 10).\
\
Spell Power can be raised through enchantments at the Arcane Altar, and is exposed as an entity attribute so equipment and other mods can modify it through the standard attribute system.

The Arcane Altar offers three enchantments exclusive to Build-A-Spell.\
\
Unlike vanilla enchantments, these have no level cap: you can enchant the same piece of armor or tool repeatedly, stacking the effect higher each time.

Each successive level costs more experience than the last, scaling in tiers.\
\
Early levels are cheap, but high-level enchantments require significant experience investment.\
\
The three enchantments are: Mana Pool (+10 maximum mana per level), Mana Regeneration (+2 mana per second per level), and Spell Power (+5 Spell Power per level).

Each spell's mana cost is calculated by adding the base costs of the delivery method, all effects, and all modifiers.\
\
The total is then multiplied by the server's global cost multiplier and any per-component cost multipliers set in the config.

Every player has a mana pool that fuels spell casting.\
\
The base mana pool holds 100 mana points and regenerates at a rate of 5 mana per second.\
\
The mana bar HUD can be toggled with the M key.

Mana regenerates passively over time based on your Mana Regen attribute.\
\
The default rate of 5 per second can be increased through the Mana Regeneration enchantment at the Arcane Altar.\
\
Regeneration is continuous: your pool refills steadily whether you are casting or not.
book.spell_guidebook.buildaspell.name: Arcane Codex
book.spell_guidebook.buildaspell.spell_e:
The most basic offensive spell effect.\
\
Deals direct damage to the target based on your Spell Power attribute.\
\
At only 5 base mana, it is the cheapest effect in the game and serves as the foundation for many combat spells.

Creates an explosion at the target location.\
\
The most expensive direct damage effect at 60 base mana.\
\
Blast power grows with each Increased Power stack (Increased Area adds a little too).\
\
Use with caution: at two or more Increased Power stacks the blast starts breaking blocks.\
\
Nullify protects creatures from the blast, not the terrain.

Strikes the target with a bolt of lightning, dealing heavy damage and setting them on fire.\
\
At 55 base mana it is expensive, but devastating.\
\
Lightning strikes can also transform mobs (e.g., villagers to witches, creepers to charged creepers) just like natural lightning.

Heal (35 mana) restores health to the target, with the amount scaling with Spell Power.\
\
Shield (45 mana) grants temporary absorption hearts that take damage before your real health.\
\
Shield is more expensive but proactive: apply it before entering combat.

Invisibility (30 mana) makes the target invisible, hiding their nameplate and model.\
\
Cleanse (20 mana) removes all negative status effects from the target: a cheap and essential defensive tool.\
\
Use Cleanse on Self delivery for a quick emergency purge.

Regenerate (35 mana) grants the Regeneration effect, healing the target steadily over time rather than all at once like Heal.\
\
It is ideal for sustained fights and recovers more total health for the mana when the buff is allowed to run its full duration.

Saturation (20 mana) restores food points, keeping you fed during long adventures.\
\
Speed (25 mana) applies the Speed effect for faster movement.\
\
Haste (25 mana) applies the Haste effect for faster mining and attack speed.\
\
All durations scale with the Prolonged modifier.

Strengthen (30 mana) grants the Strength effect for increased melee damage.\
\
Resist (35 mana) grants Resistance, reducing all incoming damage.\
\
Both potency and duration scale with Increased Power and Prolonged.\
\
Cast on Self before a fight, or on an ally to bolster them.

Grapple yanks you toward the point you are aiming at, with a slight upward lift to help you clear ledges.\
\
It is a mobility spell for the caster rather than a force applied to enemies: aim at a distant block or rooftop and pull yourself across the gap.\
\
Strength scales with Increased Power.

Gust unleashes a cone of wind in the direction you face, shoving every entity in front of you outward.\
\
Unlike Push, which radiates from an impact point, Gust is directional: sweep groups off ledges or create breathing room.\
\
Force scales with Increased Power and the cone reaches further with Increased Area.

Levitation (25 mana) applies the Levitation effect, causing the target to float upward uncontrollably.\
\
Slow Fall (15 mana) applies Slow Falling, allowing a gentle descent.\
\
Casters who master the interplay of rising and falling are said to have touched true flight.\
\
Experiment.

Push (25 mana) knocks the target away from the impact point with considerable force.\
\
Pull (25 mana) does the opposite, dragging the target toward the impact point.\
\
Both are useful for battlefield control and can be combined with other effects for devastating combos.

Yeet (30 mana) sends the target flying in the direction the target itself is facing.\
\
Launch (35 mana) propels the target straight up into the air.\
\
Slam (30 mana) smashes the target into the ground.\
\
These effects scale with Spell Power for greater force.

Blind (25 mana) applies the Blindness effect, severely limiting the target's vision range.\
\
Ignite (15 mana) sets the target on fire, dealing continuous fire damage.\
\
Ignite is one of the cheapest offensive effects and pairs well with the Prolonged modifier.

Freeze (20 mana) applies a freezing effect to the target, slowing their movement and dealing periodic frost damage similar to being inside powdered snow.\
\
It is particularly effective against Blaze and Strider mobs which take extra freeze damage.

Poison (30 mana) applies the Poison effect, dealing damage over time but never killing the target.\
\
Wither (40 mana) applies the Wither effect, which deals damage over time and CAN kill.\
\
Both durations scale with the Prolonged modifier.

Root (30 mana) locks the target in place, pinning their feet so they can neither walk nor jump for a short time.\
\
It is the ultimate setup tool: root a fleeing enemy, then follow up with a slower, heavier spell.\
\
Duration scales with Prolonged.

Slow (20 mana) applies Slowness, dragging the target's movement to a crawl.\
\
Weaken (25 mana) applies Weakness, sapping the damage of their melee attacks.\
\
Both deepen with Increased Power and last longer with Prolonged.\
\
Nullify does not stop them: status effects are not damage.

Charm pacifies every mob within range: they drop whatever they were attacking and cannot pick a new target while the effect lasts, wandering in a disoriented haze instead.\
\
The pacify lasts longer when boosted with the Prolonged or Increased Power modifiers.\
\
Unlike Summon, Charm works on creatures already in the world rather than conjuring new ones.

The Summon effect conjures an allied entity at the target location.\
\
The type of entity summoned depends on the other effects and modifiers in the spell.\
\
On its own, Summon produces a basic ally.\
\
Combined with specific effects, it can summon Iron Golems, Vexes, Skeletons, or Vindicators.

Teleportation effects are key ingredients in several powerful combos.\
\
Combining teleportation with movement effects can unlock flight capabilities, while mixing with other schools produces unique synergies.\
\
Experiment with different combinations to discover hidden techniques.

Swap (45 mana) exchanges positions between the caster and the target.\
\
Mark (30 mana) places an invisible waypoint at the target location.\
\
Recall (40 mana) teleports the caster back to the most recently placed Mark.\
\
Each caster keeps one Mark at a time, and Recall returns you to its coordinates in your current dimension.

Teleport (50 mana) moves you, the caster, to wherever the spell lands.\
\
With Self delivery, you teleport forward toward where you're looking.\
\
Blink (35 mana) is a short-range instant teleport in the direction you're facing, cheaper but with limited range.

Pickup collects all dropped items in the target area and teleports them into the caster's inventory.\
\
At 15 mana, it is cheap and incredibly convenient for collecting loot after combat or mining.\
\
Scales with Increased Area to cover a larger collection radius.

Night Vision (15 mana) lets the target see clearly in the dark, while Water Breathing (15 mana) lets them breathe underwater.\
\
Both are cheap exploration utilities and last longer with the Prolonged modifier.\
\
Cast on an area to cover your whole party at once.

Break (40 mana) destroys the targeted block, dropping it as an item. It also clears spell light, which nothing else can mine.\
\
Conjure (25 mana) places a block at the target location from a configurable list of allowed blocks (default: stone, cobblestone, blackstone, dirt, grass). It builds into air and into anything a block can normally replace: light, grass, snow and water.\
\
Both scale with Increased Area for multi-block operations.

Growth (30 mana) applies bone meal to crops and plants in the target area, accelerating their growth.\
\
Reap (40 mana) harvests mature crops and automatically replants seeds.\
\
Together they form a powerful farming automation system, especially when combined with the Increased Area modifier.

Light (12 mana) fills the area around the target with invisible light sources: a radius of 5 blocks by default, wider with Increased Area. Ideal for lighting caves on the fly.\
\
The lights fade on their own after a minute, so a cast brightens a place without permanently rewriting it. The lifetime is server-configurable, and Break clears them early.\
\
Create Water (20 mana) places a water source block.\
\
Evaporate Water (25 mana) removes water source blocks.
book.spell_guidebook.buildaspell.spell_m:
Fortunate Son enriches what your spells yield.\
\
On Break, it applies Fortune to the broken block, yielding more drops from ores and other fortune-affected blocks.\
\
On Reap, it adds bonus crop drops the same way.\
\
On damage spells, it acts as Looting: creatures slain by the spell drop extra loot. Players are left alone — what they drop is their own belongings, not rolled loot.\
\
Stackable: each stack raises the fortune and looting level, up to a cap of three.\
\
Best combined with Break and Increased Area for efficient mining.

Increased Area expands the area of effect for spells that affect a region.\
\
Each stack increases the radius further.\
\
This is stackable and particularly powerful with effects like Explosion, Break, Conjure, Growth, and Reap.\
\
It is also a key component in many secret combos.

Increased Power amplifies the strength of all effects in the spell.\
\
Each stack multiplies the spell's potency further.\
\
This is a stackable modifier — add multiple copies for greater amplification.\
\
It is the go-to modifier for maximizing damage or healing output.

Accelerate (15 mana) increases projectile travel speed, making it harder for targets to dodge.\
\
Not stackable.\
\
Pierce (20 mana) allows the projectile to pass through entities, hitting every target in its path.\
\
Stackable: each stack allows one additional pass-through.

Bounce (25 mana) causes projectiles to ricochet off surfaces, potentially hitting targets around corners.\
\
Not stackable.\
\
Chain (30 mana) makes the spell jump to a nearby target after hitting the first, like chain lightning.\
\
Stackable for additional chain jumps.

Split divides a single projectile into multiple projectiles, each carrying the full spell effect.\
\
Stackable: each stack adds one more projectile to the volley.\
\
At 45 mana per stack, it is the most expensive projectile modifier but incredibly powerful for area saturation.

Fill fills the space the spell lands in, and stops where that space stops. It walks from block to touching block instead of measuring distance, so it cannot reach through a wall into a room it never touched.\
\
Conjure and Create Water pour. They settle to the floor and rise a layer at a time, so a hole fills to ground level and a sealed room fills to its ceiling. Cast somewhere genuinely open there is nothing holding the fill, and nothing is placed.\
\
Break and Evaporate Water follow the mass instead. Break clears the run of blocks it hit and stops at the open air, and Evaporate drains the body of water it was cast into and stops at its shore.\
\
Not stackable, and Increased Area does not widen it. Wall and Floor still take priority over Fill. The search reaches 30 blocks by default, which is a limit rather than a shape.\
\
The most expensive shape modifier at 40 mana.

Wall (30 mana) reshapes the spell's area of effect into a vertical wall pattern.\
\
Floor (30 mana) reshapes it into a horizontal floor pattern.\
\
Neither is stackable.\
\
These modifiers are essential for Conjure-based building spells, allowing you to create walls and floors of blocks instantly.

Double adds an extra projectile to Cast and Tracking spells.\
\
Stackable: each stack fires another projectile alongside the first.\
\
At 50 mana per stack, it is the most expensive modifier in the game.\
\
Unlike Echo, which re-casts the spell after a delay, Double delivers all its projectiles in the same instant.

Gentleness makes harvesting spells careful instead of greedy.\
\
Not stackable.\
\
On Break, blocks are collected intact as if mined with Silk Touch.\
\
On Reap, crops are gathered plainly, without Fortunate Son's bonus multiplication.\
\
At 10 mana it is very cheap: standard kit for any mining or farming spell.

Leech heals you for a fraction of the damage your spell deals to enemies.\
\
Stackable: each stack returns more of the damage as health.\
\
Attach it to a Damage spell to sustain yourself through a fight, turning offense directly into staying power.

Nullify removes all damage to creatures from the spell: Damage, Explosion, Lightning and the like hurt nothing, while everything else still happens.\
\
Status effects, knockback, ignition and block changes are untouched.\
\
Not stackable.\
\
At only 5 mana, it is the cheapest modifier.\
\
Use it to apply status effects without killing the target.\
\
It does not protect terrain: a Nullified Explosion still breaks blocks once its Increased Power climbs high enough, so keep the power low when you want a fully harmless blast.

Return makes a projectile spell boomerang back toward you after it hits or reaches the end of its flight, re-applying its effects to anything it passes on the way home.\
\
Not stackable.\
\
Only useful on projectile deliveries such as Cast and Tracking.

Sunder adds bonus damage that scales with how much armor the target is wearing.\
\
Stackable.\
\
Because spell damage already ignores armor, Sunder is your anti-tank tool: the more heavily armored the foe, the harder it bites.\
\
It does little against unarmored targets.

Duration turns the spell into a persistent area: instead of firing once, the spell lingers where it lands and re-applies its effects in steady pulses.\
\
Each stack extends how long the area lasts. It also prolongs summoned constructs and storms: blizzards, lightning storms, sanctuaries, black holes, and rune traps. This is the opposite of Prolonged, which lengthens status effects on targets rather than the zone itself.\
\
Duration is expensive, but it is the key to zone control: pulsing damage fields, healing circles, or lasting terrain effects.\
\
If the spell forms a combo, the combo takes over instead.

Echo causes the spell to re-trigger after a short delay.\
\
Stackable: each additional Echo adds another re-trigger.\
\
Each echo strikes at reduced power compared to the one before it, so echoes multiply the spell's output with diminishing returns.\
\
Excellent for sustained damage or repeated healing.

Linger makes the spell settle where it lands as a persistent area, re-applying its effects to anything inside on a steady pulse: a lingering-potion-style cloud.\
\
Unlike Duration, Linger is a cheaper one-time enabler at a fixed base lifetime. Stack Duration on top to extend how long the area lasts, and Increased Area to widen it.\
\
If the spell forms a combo, the combo takes over instead.

Prolonged (18 mana) increases the active duration of status effects applied to targets: poison, freeze, ignite, root, and the like.\
\
Stackable for longer lasting effects. It does NOT extend summoned zones or constructs; for that, see Duration.\
\
Delay (8 mana) adds a time delay before the spell activates after casting.\
\
Stackable: each copy adds more delay.\
\
Useful for timed traps.
